The `question` tool is the shared runtime contract for clarification requests, questionnaires, and pause/resume answer collection. Assistant Chat, Interview, wizard clarification, and approval-adjacent follow-up flows consume this contract rather than inventing surface-local payloads.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/assistant-chat-design.md, ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md, ContractName:Plans/interview-subagent-integration.md

#### Request shape

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `string` | yes | Presentation hint. The canonical values are `single_question` and `questionnaire`. |
| `header` | `string` | no | Short UI title for the card or modal. |
| `prompt` | `string` | yes | Shared explanatory copy for the whole request. |
| `questions[]` | `QuestionItem[]` | yes | Ordered question set. One entry still uses the same schema. |
| `context_ref?` | `string` | no | Optional evidence or artifact reference shown alongside the questionnaire. |

#### `QuestionItem`

`QuestionItem{question_id, question, options[], required, multi_select, allow_freeform, default_values}`

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `question_id` | `string` | yes | Stable identifier used across chat, storage, and resumption. |
| `question` | `string` | yes | User-facing question text. |
| `options[]` | `Array<{id, label, description?}>` | no | Canonical option shape. `string[]` input is expanded at ingestion and is not the runtime contract. |
| `required` | `boolean` | no | Defaults to `false`. |
| `multi_select` | `boolean` | no | Defaults to `false`. |
| `allow_freeform` | `boolean` | no | Allows typed input in addition to or instead of options. |
| `default_values` | `string[]` | no | Default selected option ids or freeform defaults. |

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/assistant-chat-design.md, ContractName:Plans/chain-wizard-flexibility.md

#### Answer and outcome shape

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `question_id` | `string` | Stable question identifier. |
| `selected_option_ids[]?` | `string[]` | Present for selection or mixed responses. |
| `freeform_text?` | `string` | Present for freeform or mixed responses. |
| `response_kind` | `selection | freeform | mixed` | Canonical answer discriminator. |
| `validation_state` | `valid | invalid | pending` | Validation result at save or submit time. |
| `answered_at_utc?` | `string` | Durable timestamp for completed answers. |

Request-level lifecycle states are `answered`, `submitted`, `dismissed`, `timed_out`, and `unavailable`.

#### Runtime rules

- navigation may move out of order; the runtime does not force one-card-at-a-time sequencing
- required questions gate final submit until all required items are complete and locally valid
- draft answers auto-save, pause, and resume without fabricating a submitted result
- dismiss pauses the flow; it does not synthesize success
- timeout and unavailable are first-class outcomes surfaced to chat/storage/consumers

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md, ContractName:Plans/FinalGUISpec.md

`todoread` and `todowrite` expose one normalized planning/TODO schema shared by Assistant Chat, planning widgets, storage, and delegated execution.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/assistant-chat-design.md, ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md, ContractName:Plans/Run_Modes.md

#### Canonical TODO item

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `todo_id` | `string` | yes | Stable identifier. |
| `title` | `string` | yes | Short actionable label. |
| `summary` | `string` | no | Optional user-facing detail. |
| `status` | `pending | in_progress | completed | blocked | skipped` | yes | Canonical status set. |
| `dependencies[]` | `string[]` | no | Upstream `todo_id` values. |
| `owner_hint` | `string` | no | Optional surface or worker hint. |
| `verification_hint` | `string` | no | Optional verification reminder. |

#### Operation rules

- `todoread` returns the ordered normalized list plus dependency metadata
- `todowrite` applies item-level upsert, reorder, dependency, and status updates against the same schema
- markdown planning artifacts that drive execution must update the normalized TODO projection before execution begins
- every durable mutation emits `chat.plan_todo_updated`

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md, ContractName:Plans/assistant-chat-design.md

The canonical web tool family comprises six first-class built-in tools: `websearch`, `webfetch`, `webextract`, `webresearch`, `webcrawl`, and `webmap`. All six share provider routing, provenance disclosure, blocked-payload projection, and audit storage.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md, ContractName:Plans/assistant-chat-design.md, ContractName:Plans/Contracts_V0.md

#### Shared request fields

| Field | Type | Used by | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `adapter_hint` | `string?` | all | Optional preferred provider or adapter. |
| `include_domains[]` | `string[]` | search, research, crawl, map | Domain allow filter. |
| `exclude_domains[]` | `string[]` | search, research, crawl, map | Domain deny filter. |
| `cache_policy` | `object?` | fetch, extract, research, crawl, map | Consumer override of PM cache behavior. |
| `task` | `string?` | research | Short execution goal shown in activity cards. |
| `depth_hint` | `quick | standard | deep` | research | Search/read iteration hint. |
| `auto_read_cap` | `integer?` | research | Maximum automatic reads in PM-composed mode. |
| `schema` | `object?` | extract | Canonical extraction schema. |
| `schema_mode` | `strict | lenient` | extract | Validation behavior. |
| `root_url` | `string?` | crawl, map | Canonical site root when distinct from the starting URL. |

#### Shared output and audit fields

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `provider_id` | Effective provider used for the operation. |
| `effective_provider_mode` | One of the capability/routing modes defined in the provider matrix. |
| `web_operation` | Canonical operation name. |
| `web_input` | Structured normalized request snapshot. |
| `cache_state` | `hit`, `miss`, `bypassed`, or `expired_used_for_diff`. |
| `sources_ref?` / `content_ref?` / `map_ref?` / `answer_summary_ref?` | Durable evidence references projected by storage. |

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md, ContractName:Plans/Tools.md#11-provider-capability-matrix

#### Per-tool contract summary

| Tool | Required input | Locked defaults / special rules | Output emphasis | Extra error families |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `websearch` | `query` | `max_results` defaults to `10`; domain filters are optional | ranked result list + provider disclosure | `unsupported_source` |
| `webfetch` | `url` | Site Reader remains the primary path when it satisfies the request; action-bearing fetches bypass lookup | content + metadata + optional diff refs | consumer uses owner taxonomy in `Plans/Contracts_V0.md` |
| `webextract` | `url`, optional `schema` | canonical extraction target is `/v2/extract`, not `/scrape` | structured extraction + validation result | `extraction_schema_mismatch` |
| `webresearch` | `query` | PM-composed by default; `auto_read_cap` and `depth_hint` bound autonomous behavior | answer summary + source set + methodology | `autonomous_budget_exceeded` |
| `webcrawl` | `url` | bounded recursive crawl; default bounds are finite and user-visible | page set + crawl stats | `content_blocked`, `content_not_found` |
| `webmap` | `url` | bounded URL discovery; default bounds are finite and user-visible | discovered URL set + sitemap metadata | `content_not_found` |

#### `WebAction` type definition

A `WebAction` is a sequential browser-interaction step executed before extraction or readback. The canonical enum is:

`click | scroll | type | press_key | wait_for | navigate | screenshot | set_viewport | fill_form | select_option | back | reload | snapshot | console | network`

Runtime rules:
- actions execute in order
- the wall-clock budget for one action list is capped at 30s
- failure stops subsequent actions for that request
- per-action status is still returned so partial progress remains visible

#### Error ownership

The canonical web error taxonomy lives in `Plans/Contracts_V0.md`. This section consumes that taxonomy and does not publish a competing owner list. Exact web-only codes that must remain visible to implementers include `adapter_unavailable`, `unsupported_operation`, `content_blocked`, `content_not_found`, `unsupported_source`, `extraction_schema_mismatch`, `autonomous_budget_exceeded`, and `no_previous_version`.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Contracts_V0.md, ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md

MCP canon is owned by `Plans/MCP_Integration.md`. This section is a consumer cross-reference for tool-registry and permission integration only.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/MCP_Integration.md, ContractName:Plans/Permissions_System.md, ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md

Consumer rules:
- requested versus effective MCP availability is resolved through the owner document; this section does not redefine it
- credential binding and invalidation semantics are owner-defined in `Plans/MCP_Integration.md`
- tool names use the underscore-only form `{server_slug}_{tool_name}`

anchors.anchor: ### 8.6 MCP tool name format and wildcard rule
anchors.content_markdown:
MCP tool names use the owner-defined underscore-only format `{server_slug}_{tool_name}`.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/MCP_Integration.md

Rules:
- wildcard rules match the underscore form, for example `context7_*`
- slash variants and mixed `_` / `/` examples are retired

Canonical defaults are owned by `Plans/Permissions_System.md` §7. This consumer summary keeps the tool-registry view aligned to that owner table.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Permissions_System.md

| Tool family | Default |
|---|---|
| `skill` | `allow` |
| `question` | `allow` only when HITL is available; otherwise `ask` |
| `websearch`, `webfetch`, `webextract`, `webresearch`, `webcrawl`, `webmap` | `ask` |

Preset semantics are owned by `Plans/Permissions_System.md` §10.4. This section preserves the tool-registry mapping without restating conflicting policy.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Permissions_System.md

| Preset | Tool-facing effect |
|---|---|
| `read_only` | read/search/list style tools stay available; mutation stays denied |
| `plan` | planning helpers stay available, read-only web tools remain `ask`, and no preset silently auto-denies the whole web family |
| `full` | broad availability with explicit asks on mutation-capable tools |

Child-agent denial of `question` is architectural and remains in force even when the parent preset is broader.

Firecrawl is a distinct provider in PM's web stack. The provider contract below covers configuration, endpoint mapping, native batch behavior, async polling, and disclosure requirements. Consumer summaries in other docs defer to this owner section.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/CLI_Bridged_Providers.md, ContractName:Plans/Models_System.md, ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md

### 10.1 Provider configuration

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `bool` | Provider availability flag. |
| `api_key` | `secret_ref?` | API credential reference. |
| `base_url` | `string` | Supports hosted and self-hosted deployments. |
| `timeout_ms` | `integer` | Default request timeout. |
| `proxy_mode` | `direct | pm_proxy | provider_managed` | Network routing choice. |
| `cache_enabled` | `bool` | Enables provider cache hints in addition to PM cache. |

### 10.2 Endpoint inventory

Firecrawl-native endpoints that PM maps to are:
- `/v2/scrape`
- `/v2/crawl`
- `/v2/map`
- `/v2/search`
- `/v2/extract`
- `/v2/batch/scrape`
- `/v2/agent`

### 10.3 PM → Firecrawl operation mapping

| PM operation | Firecrawl endpoint | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `webfetch` | `/v2/scrape` | PM may still prefer Site Reader when that path satisfies the request. |
| `webextract` | `/v2/extract` | Never `/scrape`. |
| `webcrawl` | `/v2/crawl` | Native crawl job / async flow. |
| `webmap` | `/v2/map` | Native URL discovery. |
| `websearch` | `/v2/search` | Search provider path when selected by routing. |
| `batch_webfetch` / `batch_webextract` | `/v2/batch/scrape` and extraction follow-on | Native batch behavior stays visible. |
| provider-native research | `/v2/agent` | Used only when routing explicitly chooses provider-native agent mode. |

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Tools.md#12-web-tool-routing-algorithm

### 10.4 Async jobs, polling, and cache hints

- long-running Firecrawl jobs use provider-native polling with bounded backoff
- PM records the effective polling state and job handle in audit payloads when native async is used
- provider cache hints such as `storeInCache` and `minAge` remain hints beneath PM cache precedence rather than replacing the PM cache contract

### 10.5 Credit, source, and self-hosted disclosure

- credit-bearing paths disclose estimated cost before provider-native agent escalation when the estimate exceeds 100 credits
- PM surfaces provider-source disclosure whenever routing selected Firecrawl rather than a PM-native path
- self-hosted deployments may not support every hosted capability; PM marks unsupported operations as `partial` or `unsupported` in the provider matrix instead of overstating native parity

### 10.6 Research and browser-session alignment

Firecrawl may back `research_session`-adjacent flows, but `research_session` remains a PM-owned runtime model. Firecrawl support does not collapse PM's `research_session` into a provider-owned browser runtime.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Section15_MVP_Promoted_Features_Spec.md, ContractName:Plans/Permissions_System.md

This matrix exposes PM's effective support tier by provider and operation. The capability value is reported per operation rather than as one flattened provider adjective.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Models_System.md, ContractName:Plans/CLI_Bridged_Providers.md

Capability values:
- `native`
- `near-native`
- `native (model)`
- `native (agent)`
- `pm-composed`
- `partial`
- `unsupported`

| Provider / surface | `websearch` | `webfetch` | `webextract` | `webresearch` | `webcrawl` | `webmap` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PM Site Reader | `unsupported` | `native` | `pm-composed` | `pm-composed` | `unsupported` | `unsupported` |
| Firecrawl | `native` | `native` | `native` | `native (agent)` or `pm-composed` | `native` | `native` |
| Tavily / search-style providers | `native` | `unsupported` | `unsupported` | `pm-composed` | `unsupported` | `unsupported` |
| model-native browser/tooling | `partial` | `near-native` | `partial` | `native (model)` or `pm-composed` | `partial` | `partial` |

Consumer rules:
- same-operation fallback only; PM does not silently replace one web operation with another
- support-tier disclosure remains visible in UI and activity cards
- health and last-failure state participate in routing; they are not hidden diagnostic metadata

Routing chooses the effective provider without changing the requested operation. The algorithm below is the canonical owner flow for all six web tools and the batch variants.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/assistant-chat-design.md, ContractName:Plans/Models_System.md, ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md

1. normalize the requested operation and input shape
2. if the request is `webfetch` and Site Reader can satisfy it, prefer `Reading Site`
3. build candidate providers for the same requested operation only
4. filter candidates by parameter support, including action support and extraction schema support
5. filter candidates by health / availability and requested-vs-effective account state
6. apply user or policy hints such as `adapter_hint`, domain filters, and self-hosting constraints
7. evaluate cost and credit posture; warn before high-cost provider-native agent paths
8. choose the lowest-cost healthy candidate that satisfies the requested operation without semantic downgrade
9. record fallback chain, effective provider, support tier, and user-visible activity label

Activity labels are routing-aware:
- `Reading Site`
- `Extracting Site`
- `Researching Web`
- `Crawling Site`
- `Mapping Site`

Special routing rules:
- action-bearing `webfetch` bypasses cache lookup before provider selection
- bare `/web` never hard-routes to search; the slash layer resolves help/autocomplete first
- provider-native research is opt-in, not the default meaning of `webresearch`

PM exposes two canonical batch tools: `batch_webfetch` and `batch_webextract`. They preserve per-URL routing, permissions, provenance, and cache semantics while presenting one grouped tool result.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/assistant-chat-design.md, ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md, ContractName:Plans/Permissions_System.md

### 13.1 Batch contract

| Tool | Input | Limits | Success rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `batch_webfetch` | `urls[]`, shared read options | bounded URL list | success when at least one URL succeeds |
| `batch_webextract` | `urls[]`, `schema`, extraction options | bounded URL list | success when at least one URL yields a valid extraction |

Runtime rules:
- timeout budget is `individual_timeout × min(url_count, 5)` with a hard cap of `600s`
- permission review uses one confirmation surface listing unique domains
- each URL still performs independent routing, audit emission, and cache handling
- partial completion is explicit: `partial_results: true`
- cancellation preserves already-completed URL results and returns `cancelled`

### 13.2 Progress and result payloads

Progress payloads emit `progress_event` records with `tool_use_id`, completed count, total count, and the current URL when available.

Result payload:
- `items[]` with one entry per URL
- `succeeded_count`
- `failed_count`
- `partial_results`
- `provider_summary`
- evidence refs for any stored content or extraction outputs

Web caching is PM-owned and storage-backed. Provider caches are subordinate hints beneath this contract.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md

#### Canonical cache identity

The cache key is `(normalized_url, formats_hash, adapter_id)`.

#### Rules

- action-bearing fetches bypass lookup because action lists are semantically material to page state
- PM cache lookup precedes provider cache hints
- invalidation is available by URL, domain, and project scope
- stale content may be reused for diff generation and is reported as `expired_used_for_diff`
- disk-backed storage survives restart with a default per-project ceiling of `500 MB`

#### State vocabulary

`hit`, `miss`, `bypassed`, `expired_used_for_diff`

#### Provider hints

Firecrawl-specific cache hints such as `storeInCache` and `minAge` remain provider-level knobs. They do not replace PM cache keying, precedence, invalidation, or state vocabulary.

Assistant Chat reserves one built-in slash-command set. The canonical built-ins are:

`/new`, `/model`, `/effort`, `/mode`, `/export`, `/compact`, `/stop`, `/resume`, `/rewind`, `/revert`, `/share`, `/settings`, `/doctor`, `/help`, and `/web`

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Commands_System.md, ContractName:Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md

- `/clear` is removed from live canon
- no delete-message command survives in chat canon
- built-in ownership lives in `Plans/Commands_System.md`; this section is the chat consumer surface

`/web` and `/skill` are entry affordances, but they do not redefine the underlying owner contracts.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Commands_System.md, ContractName:Plans/Skills_System.md, ContractName:Plans/Tools.md

#### `/web`

- bare `/web` opens help and autocomplete for the web tool family
- bare `/web` has no default operation and does not silently mean search
- operation-specific invocations still resolve into the canonical six-tool web family

#### `/skill`

- bare `/skill` lists and helps discover invokable skills
- `/skill` is a discovery and invocation surface, not an “open panel” command
- runtime invocation still flows through the structured skill contract in `Plans/Skills_System.md`

Assistant Chat consumes the shared `question` runtime contract rather than defining a chat-local payload shape.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Tools.md, ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md, ContractName:Plans/FinalGUISpec.md

#### Question card UI

The chat surface renders one shared request shape:
- `mode`
- `header`
- `prompt`
- `questions[]`

Each `questions[]` entry uses the canonical `QuestionItem{question_id, question, options[], required, multi_select, allow_freeform, default_values}` contract.

#### Interaction rules

- multi-question questionnaires may be navigated out of order
- required items gate submit
- drafts auto-save and resume
- dismiss pauses rather than inventing an answer
- first-class request outcomes are `answered`, `submitted`, `dismissed`, `timed_out`, and `unavailable`

#### Answer payload alignment

Chat consumer payloads preserve `response_kind` and `validation_state`; they do not rename them into chat-local fields.

Assistant Chat owns the user-facing planning model and its TODO vocabulary. Storage and tool sections consume this owner shape.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md, ContractName:Plans/Tools.md, ContractName:Plans/Run_Modes.md

#### Canonical TODO item

`todo_id`, `title`, `summary`, `status`, `dependencies[]`, `owner_hint`, `verification_hint`

`status` uses:
- `pending`
- `in_progress`
- `completed`
- `blocked`
- `skipped`

#### Planning rules

- markdown planning artifacts that drive execution must update the normalized TODO projection before execution begins
- every durable item mutation emits `chat.plan_todo_updated`
- Deep Plan remains a question-driven planning loop rather than a silent background rewrite
- plan and Deep Plan share the same normalized TODO projection even when the visible artifact is markdown

Operation cards expose durable execution state, recovery affordances, and narrative ordering for chat-visible work.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md, ContractName:Plans/FinalGUISpec.md, ContractName:Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md

Canonical card statuses:
- `pending`
- `running`
- `completed`
- `failed`
- `cancelled`
- `blocked`

Blocked cards surface:
- `blocked_reason_code`
- ordered `allowed_action_ids[]`
- headless-safe recovery actions when no terminal or browser surface is attached

Terminal action taxonomy remains distinct:
- `Open in Terminal`
- `Show Terminal`
- `Rerun in Terminal`
- `Detach/Pop-Out`

Narrative ordering keeps the card family in the conversation flow rather than moving state into a hidden activity rail.

Chat-visible web activity reflects routing and provenance rather than flattening all reads into one provider label.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Tools.md, ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md

Canonical activity labels:
- `Reading Site`
- `Extracting Site`
- `Researching Web`
- `Crawling Site`
- `Mapping Site`

Visible provenance fields:
- requested operation
- effective provider
- support tier
- cache state
- evidence refs (`sources_ref`, `content_ref`, `map_ref`, `answer_summary_ref`) when available

Blocked web notices consume the storage-owned fields `blocked_reason_code`, `allowed_action_ids[]`, `web_operation`, and structured `web_input`.

anchors.anchor: ## 28. Markdown and Mermaid Rendering in Chat and Planning Surfaces (2026-03-07)
anchors.content_markdown:
Chat and planning surfaces support both Mermaid and the broader inline visualizer, but they are distinct contracts.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/FinalGUISpec.md, ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md

### 28.1 Canonical split

- Mermaid remains the fenced-diagram rendering path
- the inline visualizer is a separate sandboxed HTML/SVG module
- neither path owns hidden mutable state outside durable source or metadata refs

### 28.2 Inline visualizer bridge

The inline visualizer bridge exposes:
- `sendPrompt`
- `openLink`

Rules:
- bridge calls are sandboxed and scoped to the rendered module
- source and metadata persistence are durable; hidden JS-heap state is not
- fallback and error states are explicit rather than silently collapsing into Mermaid

The unified Settings panel owns provider, account, model, and permission configuration. It does not re-own Personas or Skills.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Skills_System.md, ContractName:Plans/Permissions_System.md, ContractName:Plans/Models_System.md

Required surfaces:
- provider class disclosure: `account-backed`, `API-backed`, `no-key`
- requested versus effective account / provider state
- support-tier and health / last-failure disclosure for web-capable providers
- credit/cost warning UI for high-cost provider-native research paths

Agent Config owns Personas and Skills. Settings owns providers/accounts/models/permissions.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Skills_System.md, ContractName:Plans/Personas.md

Required Agent Config surfaces:
- Persona selection and editing
- skill registry with source vocabulary `bundled`, `pm_enhanced`, `catalog_installed`, `manual_import`, `project_local`, `global_local`, `shadowed`
- readiness vocabulary `ready`, `ready_with_warnings`, `invalid`, `shadowed`, `disabled`
- invocation/help affordances that align with `/skill`

V1 import rules:
- Git URL import is not part of MVP
- import/install flows stay within the supported skill surfaces defined by `Plans/Skills_System.md`

anchors.anchor: ## 15. Promoted widget catalog (web tools, planning, question, operation cards)
anchors.content_markdown:
The promoted widget catalog mirrors the shared runtime contracts. Widget entries below replace the older mixed status taxonomy and the Mermaid-only collapse.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/assistant-chat-design.md, ContractName:Plans/Tools.md, ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md

### 15.1 Terminal operation card widget

Statuses: `pending`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `blocked`

Actions:
- `Open in Terminal`
- `Show Terminal`
- `Rerun in Terminal`
- `Detach/Pop-Out`

### 15.2 Search result card widget

Shows routed provider disclosure, support tier, and evidence refs without collapsing the underlying requested operation.

### 15.3 Web/diff operation card widget

Displays `web_operation`, effective provider, cache state, and blocked recovery fields when present.

### 15.4 Planning panel widget (sticky sidebar)

Consumes the normalized TODO schema:
`todo_id`, `title`, `summary`, `status`, `dependencies[]`, `owner_hint`, `verification_hint`

### 15.5 Question card widget

Renders the shared `QuestionItem` contract, supports out-of-order navigation, draft resume, required gating, and the request outcomes `answered`, `submitted`, `dismissed`, `timed_out`, `unavailable`.

### 15.6 Mermaid / inline visualizer widget

Mermaid and inline visualizer are separate renderers. The inline visualizer uses the sandboxed bridge `sendPrompt` / `openLink` and explicit fallback/error states.

### 15.7 Permission approval card widget

Uses the four-step ladder `deny`, `once`, `for session`, `always`, plus visible blocked recovery context through `blocked_reason_code` and `allowed_action_ids[]`.

Tool permission ownership lives here. The keys below are the canonical permission surface for the web, question, skill, task, and MCP families touched by this packet.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Tools.md, ContractName:Plans/MCP_Integration.md

| Permission key | Applies to | Default |

Ask resolution uses one four-step ladder and one durable snapshot model.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md, ContractName:Plans/assistant-chat-design.md, ContractName:Plans/Tools.md

### 6.1 Approval ladder

The canonical choices are:
- `deny`
- `once`
- `for session`
- `always`

### 6.2 Shared rules

- deny cascades across materially related pending approvals from the same blocked episode
- approval snapshots freeze into the active run and re-snapshot only on explicit reroute / retry / resume boundaries
- `for session` on a parent web approval unlocks Tier 2 `research_session` actions for that same session without a second confirmation
- batch approval shows unique domains once rather than per URL

### 6.5 Four-tier approval ladder

The ladder above replaces older three-option phrasing. Consumer surfaces must not retain `allow/deny/ask` or other shorter approval menus as the user-facing resolution model.

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|

| `unsupported_operation` | the selected provider does not support the requested operation |
| `content_blocked` | the source is blocked by policy, robots, auth, or similar gating |
| `content_not_found` | the requested page/resource/site content does not exist |

# MCP Integration

This document is the single SSOT for PM MCP configuration, naming, availability, credential binding, and invalidation.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Tools.md, ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md, ContractName:Plans/Permissions_System.md

## 1. Canonical naming

MCP tools use the underscore-only form `{server_slug}_{tool_name}`.

Rules:
- slash-separated aliases are not canonical
- wildcard rules match the underscore form

## 2. Requested versus effective availability

MCP state is disclosed in both requested and effective form.

Required fields:
- requested server enablement
- effective server availability
- requested tool access
- effective tool availability
- last failure / degraded state when applicable

## 3. Credential binding and invalidation

Credential state is part of the effective MCP contract rather than an implementation footnote.

Rules:
- server credentials bind to the server identity that used them
- invalid or rotated credentials invalidate effective availability until revalidated
- consumers cross-reference this owner contract rather than restating their own credential rules

## 4. Cross-surface responsibilities

- `Plans/Tools.md` consumes MCP naming and tool-registry behavior
- `Plans/storage-plan.md` consumes availability / audit projection fields
- `Plans/Permissions_System.md` consumes permission-key behavior
- `Plans/newtools.md` and GUI summaries reference this document as the live SSOT
